statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F = 3 xz\vec i + y\vec k through the surface S, which is the hemisphere x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 9, z \geq 0, oriented upward.

static.solution: z=\sqrt{9 - x^2 - y^2}, so z_x = -\frac{x}{\sqrt{9 -x^2-y^2}} \quad z_y = -\frac{y}{\sqrt{9 -x^2-y^2}}. Thus \vec F\cdot\vec A = \left(3 x\sqrt{9 - x^2-y^2}\vec i + y\vec k\right) \cdot \left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{9 -x^2-y^2}}\vec i + \frac{y}{\sqrt{9 -x^2-y^2}}\vec j + \vec k\right) = 3 x^2 + y. The flux integral is then given by \int_S \vec F \cdot d\vec A = \int_S 3 x^2 + y\,dx\,dy = \int_{-3}^{3}\int_{-\sqrt{9-x^2}}^{\sqrt{9-x^2}}(3 x^2 + y)\,dy\,dx Changing to polar coordinates gives \int_S \vec F \cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{3} (3 r^2\cos^2\theta + r\sin\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta, so that \int_S \vec F \cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi} \left(\frac{243}{4}\cos^2\theta + 9\sin\theta\right)\,d\theta = \frac{243}{4} \pi.
